prerequisites: Prior knowledge of mechanics, elasticity theory, and strength of materials is recommended.
These topics are covered in the courses: Mechanics and Theory of Mechanisms (2nd year, 2nd semester) and Elasticity and Strength of Materials (3rd year, 1st semester).

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to elasto-plastic behavior under uniaxial load
Yield criteria for the ideal plastic solid: Tresca and Von-Mises criteria. Yield criteria dependent on hydrostatic pressure: Mohr-Coulomb criterion.
Incremental theory: Levy-Mises equations and Prandtl-Reuss equations.
Phenomena of plastic behavior dependent on time.
Mechanical strength of structures with defects. Methodology of fracture mechanics. Damage tolerance.
Energy criterion for fracture: energy release rate and specific fracture energy.
Tensile criterion for fracture: fracture toughness.
Mechanical design of shafts and axles

assessment_methods.method: Written final exam on all syllabus topics

assessment_rules: The course uses continuous evaluation. The final written exam (60%), laboratory practice exam (10%), and computer lab practicals (15%) are re-evaluable and require a minimum score of 4 out of 10. The problem set (10%) and laboratory practice report and work (5%) are not re-evaluable. Students failing in the ordinary call may resit only the re-evaluable activities, and 100% attendance is mandatory for practicals to be evaluated.
